issue_context.title: Add Function Pointer support to Native AOT Reflection
issue_context.body:
Once https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/69273 is in for CoreClr, Native AOT should uptake that. It is expected that the CoreClr implementation will be for V7.

See also https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/71095 for Mono.

review_comments: This was forced because an IL test was asserting the compiler. This is invalid per ECMA-335.

This should be covered in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/design/specs/Ecma-335-Augments.md#3-custom-modifiers-can-go-in-more-places-than-specified

Make the same change for ArraySignature below?
I _think_ this is thread safe, but I wanted to call this out.
I'll add an else branch that throws on non-ecma. This is never reached for non-ecma.
It looks wasteful to use the expensive parsing method that creates `Stack`, etc. Can we have `bool` on the parser that tracks whether we have encountered any modifiers?
(Or make the expensive parsing method cheaper, e.g. use inline storage for stack of limited depth.)

The modifiers handling within the type system is utter garbage. The Stack should be rewritten to use a stack-based linked list once C# can express that (I haven't been keeping track with all the `unscoped ref` stuff - maybe it can already express it). I don't think it makes sense to add extra complexity to the already incomprehensible modifiers handling if we know we'll be able to get rid of this cost.

We already pay this cost when parsing method signatures. I've never seen it in profiles.

This is never reached for non-ecma methods. There is an else branch that throws NotImplemented. There's no scenario for non-ECMA metadata generation.

All of this should be eventually rewritten to work on top of S.R.Metadata instead of the type system.
